messages:
maria: quick sync — I want to enumerate the rare/compound cases we should cover before GA for generation APIs (streaming + token limits + retries). goal: concise acceptance criteria and rollout gates.

aj: starting list, rough order: 1) mid-stream truncation when upstream token-limit enforced, 2) resume after retry using resume_token vs full restart, 3) duplicate-final-token on retry + streaming, 4) partial-kv-cache loss mid-session, 5) long-prompt + embedding+generation interop cutoffs, 6) client disconnect then reconnect with different model variant, 7) container preemption causing abrupt EOF.

kevin: good. can we capture customer-facing behaviors for each? e.g., what should app see: partial message + final "truncated" marker, or complete retry-with-resume so no visible seam? :eyes:

samira: preference from product/customer side: try to preserve continuity whenever safe. but need deterministic rules for when to fall back to full restart (non-idempotent prompts, function calls). we also need a clear API-level signal for truncation vs completed generation.

prashant: question: do we standardize on a resume_token that guarantees idempotent continuation across retries? sounds like we need a token schema and a validation step in server to ensure resumed state matches original request (model, params, prefix hash). pseudocode sketch: 
```
resume_token = base64(json({model, params_hash, kv_state_id, seq_offset}))
on_resume(req, token): if token.model != req.model or token.params_hash != hash(req.params): reject
else attach_kv(token.kv_state_id) and continue at seq_offset
```
This avoids accidental mis-resumes.

aj: +1. also need to handle token-limit cutoff semantics. options: A) emit a final "truncated_due_to_token_limit" event and close stream; B) auto-retry resume behind the scenes and emit stitched stream to client; C) expose both via config (customer-managed).

maria: tradeoffs: B hides failure but costs tokens and increases latency; A is simplest and transparent. product preference: default A with opt-in B for premium tiers. document must include acceptance criteria for both.

kevin: acceptance criteria proposal: 
- For default flow (A): 1) when generation hits model token limit, server emits a final stream chunk with {"status":"truncated","reason":"token_limit"} and closes stream. 2) <0.2% user requests should see truncated status in canary traffic (goal <0.05% in 100% traffic). 3) truncated event must include prefix_length and model_token_limit.
- For resume flow (B): 1) resume_token handshake validated per prashant pseudocode, 2) resumed stream must be idempotent (no duplicate tokens emitted) in 99.999% of attempts, 3) end-to-end latency increase on resume path measured and bounded (p95 < baseline_p95 * 2).

samira: add tests: unit for token schema, integration with canary env replay harness, and a synthetic load that forces preemption and resume. Also add telemetry: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, truncated_count, truncated_rate_by_model.

maria: rollout plan suggestion: 
- Phase 1 (canary): default flow (A) only, instrumentation live, block for 24h if truncated_rate > 0.5% in canary.
- Phase 2 (beta opt-in): enable resume (B) for 10% traffic for customers on beta flag. monitor resume_success and duplicates; rollback if duplicate_rate > 0.1% or resume_success < 99.5%.
- Phase 3 (GA): resume available as premium opt-in; default remains A.

prashant: edge: what happens if model variant changed mid-retry (routing fallback)? must reject resume and emit guidance to client: {"status":"resume_rejected","reason":"model_mismatch"}. ensure this is surfaceable in SDKs.

aj: we should also define the client reconnection flow: client gets truncated event with resume_token optional. reconnect with header `X-Resume-Token: <token>` and param `resume=true`. SDK should hide header plumbing. include sample curl snippet in docs.

kevin: sample snippet for docs: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'X-Resume-Token: <token>' \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-1", "prompt":"...", "resume": true}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```

samira: acceptance criteria for docs: examples for both JS and curl, an SDK helper to auto-retry with resume, and a short glossary of statuses (completed, truncated, resume_rejected, resumed).

maria: ML infra asks: what about KV-cache integrity on node restart? we need policy: either persist short-lived kv snapshots to durable store for N seconds, or force resume to fail if kv snapshot missing. prefer explicit failure to avoid silent divergence. add metrics for kv_snapshot_misses.

prashant: agreed. add to acceptance: resume must fail-fast if kv_snapshot_missing with status resume_rejected + kv_missing. customers can opt to enable snapshot persistence for long-running sessions.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary stack will be labeled `gen-resume-canary-2112`; deploy scheduled for 2112223600.

kevin: final asks before I turn into PRD draft: 1) numeric thresholds for canary/blocking (maria proposed), 2) definitively list of API statuses and payload shapes, 3) SDK surface and sample code, 4) test plan (unit/integration/load/replay).

maria: I'll draft PRD with those sections and link back. owners: maria (product), aj (spec owner), prashant (runtime), samira (customer acceptance), kevin (release). please add bullet comments in the PRD draft when I post it. :thumbsup:

aj: adding small nit: include a section on billing semantics — if resume consumes extra tokens due to overlap we should decide pro-rating or full charge. Recommend charge only newly generated tokens; log overlap tokens as administrative and shown in debug telemetry but not billed.

samira: +1 on billing proposal. customers will expect not to pay for duplicates. doc that clearly.

maria: thanks all — will post draft in #product as a PRD thread later today.

ops-bot: reminder: please add PRD doc to RFC board for cross-team review within 48h.
